Shrink the text of a ggplot so that it fits a given figure size

Source: R/resize_fonts.R
resize_fonts.Rd

Finds the largest font scale at which no text of a ggplot (or of a patchwork assembly of ggplots) overlaps another text or leaves the canvas, once the figure is drawn at width x height, and returns the plot with its text resized by that scale.

Text sizes in ggplot2 are absolute (points), so whether labels overlap depends on the final figure size. resize_fonts() draws the figure off-screen at that size, measures the box of every label (rotated labels included), and searches the scale by bisection between min_scale and max_scale. Inside a knitr or Quarto chunk, width and height default to the chunk's fig-width and fig-height.

Usage

resize_fonts(
  p,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  units = c("in", "cm", "mm", "px"),
  dpi = 300,
  axis_text = TRUE,
  axis_title = TRUE,
  titles = TRUE,
  strip = TRUE,
  legend = TRUE,
  geom_text = FALSE,
  resize_all = FALSE,
  min_scale = 0.3,
  max_scale = 1,
  padding = 1,
  tolerance = 0.02,
  device = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

p

A ggplot2::ggplot object or a patchwork assembly.

width, height

(numeric, default NULL) Figure size in units. When NULL, the size is taken from the current knitr/Quarto chunk (fig.width / fig-width, in inches), or else from the open graphics device, or else defaults to 7 x 5 inches (with a message).

units

(character, default "in") Units of width and height: one of "in", "cm", "mm" or "px".

dpi

(numeric, default 300) Resolution used to convert "px".

axis_text

(logical, default TRUE) Check the axis tick labels for overlaps (and resize them, see resize_all).

axis_title

(logical, default TRUE) Check the axis titles for overlaps (and resize them).

titles

(logical, default TRUE) Check the plot title, subtitle, caption and tag, including a patchwork annotation, for overlaps (and resize them).

strip

(logical, default TRUE) Check the facet strip text for overlaps (and resize it).

legend

(logical, default TRUE) Check the legend titles and labels for overlaps (and resize them).

geom_text

(logical, default FALSE) Check the text drawn by text and label layers (geom_text(), geom_label(), ggrepel geoms) for overlaps (and resize it). Layers mapping size to a variable are never resized.

resize_all

(logical, default FALSE) When FALSE, only the categories set to TRUE above are resized, and the others keep their size. When TRUE, every text of the plot (all the categories above, geom_text included) is shrunk by the same scale, and the category arguments only choose which text is checked for overlaps.

min_scale, max_scale

(numeric, default 0.3 and 1) Range of the font scale searched. Set max_scale above 1 to also let text grow.

padding

(numeric, default 1) Minimum gap, in points, required between two labels.

tolerance

(numeric, default 0.02) Precision of the scale search.

device

(character, default NULL) Device used to measure text: "png", "pdf" or "ragg". Font metrics differ slightly between devices. When NULL, the device of the current knitr chunk (dev option) is used, or else "png".

verbose

(logical, default FALSE) Print the chosen scale and the number of overlaps found at full size.

Value

The plot p with its text resized, with the chosen scale stored in the "font_scale" attribute. A category set to FALSE is never checked, and is resized only when resize_all = TRUE.

Limitations

  • Only text drawn as plain grid text is measured: rich text from 'ggtext' or 'marquee' is resized but not checked for overlaps.

  • A single scale is applied to every selected category, which keeps the relative hierarchy of the text sizes; one crowded axis therefore shrinks all the selected text.

  • When some text still overlaps at min_scale (e.g. two labels at the same position), a warning is raised and the plot is returned at min_scale. Consider ggplot2::guide_axis() (n.dodge, angle) or wrapping labels instead.

  • Each step draws the whole figure, so large plots take a few seconds.

See also

MiscMetabar::reshape_ggplot() to wrap long titles before resizing, ggplot2::guide_axis(), ggplot2::ggsave()

Author

Adrien Taudière

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  sample = paste0("Site_forest_", sprintf("%02d", 1:12)),
  reads = c(120, 145, 110, 130, 150, 90, 160, 135, 128, 142, 99, 117)
)
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = reads)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col()

p_fit <- resize_fonts(p, width = 150, height = 80, units = "mm")
attr(p_fit, "font_scale")
#> [1] 0.5296875

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In a Quarto chunk, the size comes from the chunk options:
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
resize_fonts(p)

# A patchwork, also counting the overlaps of geom_text() labels
library(patchwork)
resize_fonts(p / p, width = 6, height = 6, geom_text = TRUE)

# Shrink every text by the same amount, but only check the axis labels
resize_fonts(
  p,
  width = 4,
  height = 3,
  axis_title = FALSE,
  titles = FALSE,
  strip = FALSE,
  legend = FALSE,
  resize_all = TRUE
)
} # }
